(h2 : formParallelogram e b c f D₁₂ D₂₃ AC BD) 
(h3 : a ≠ b) 
(h4 : b ≠ c) 
(h5 : c ≠ d) 
(h6 : Line.intersectsLine AB CD)

(h8 : Line.intersectsLine D₁₂ D₂₃) : (|(a─b)| * |(c─d)|) = (|(e─b)| * |(c─f)|) := by 
  -- Prove that the lines AB and CD are parallel.
  have h9 : ¬(AB.intersectsLine CD) := by 
    intro h
    -- If AB and CD intersect, then the parallelogram a b c d would not be valid.
    apply h1.1
    exact h
  -- Prove that the lines AC and BD are parallel.
  have h10 : ¬(AC.intersectsLine BD) := by 
    intro h
    -- If AC and BD intersect, then the parallelogram a b c d would not be valid.
    apply h1.1
    exact h
  -- Prove that the lines D₁₂ and D₂₃ are parallel.
  have h11 : ¬(D₁₂.intersectsLine D₂₃) := by 
    intro h
    -- If D₁₂ and D₂₃ intersect, then the parallelogram e b c f would not be valid.
    apply h2.1
    exact h
  -- Calculate the area of the parallelogram a b c d.
  have area1 : (|(a─b)| * |(c─d)|) = (|(c─d)| * |(a─b)|) := by 
    ring
  -- Calculate the area of the parallelogram e b c f.
  have area2 : (|(e─b)| * |(c─f)|) = (|(c─f)| * |(e─b)|) := by

nl_statement: Parallelograms which are on the same base and between the same parallels are equal to one another. I say that $ABCD$ is equal to parallelogram $EBCF$. <prf> Thus, the whole parallelogram $ABCD$ is equal to the whole parallelogram $EBCF$.Thus, parallelograms which are on the same base and between the same parallels are equal to one another.
